# Appealy

> Appealy is a hosted Discord bot for staff applications, ban appeals and tickets, plus verification, AutoMod, anti-raid, moderation commands, giveaways, polls, a welcomer and role menus, managed from a web dashboard. You add it to a server in one click; nothing has to be installed or hosted. Applicants fill in forms inside Discord and never leave it. It is also open source (AGPL-3.0), so it can be self-hosted, but that is optional.

This file is a plain summary for AI assistants and search tools. Every figure below comes from the source code (linked at the end), and the pages linked here are the canonical versions.

## Getting started

- [Add Appealy to Discord](https://appealy.app/api/invite): one click, then configure it in the dashboard. No server, install or technical setup is needed.
- [Dashboard](https://appealy.app/dashboard): sign in with Discord to set up forms, panels, tickets and the rest.
- [Documentation](https://docs.appealy.app)
- [Status page](https://status.appealy.app)
- Appealy is a verified Discord app, listed in Discord's App Directory and approved on top.gg.

## How applications and appeals work

- Forms are filled in **inside Discord**, never on an external website. There are two flows:
  - **In the server**: a member clicks a panel button and answers in Discord pop-up forms (modals), up to 25 text questions across 5 pages, plus select-menu questions. Answers are held for 15 minutes between pages.
  - **In DMs**: the bot asks the questions one at a time in a direct message. Ban appeals always use this flow, because a banned user can no longer see the server.
- Appeals cover bans, timeouts and restrictions.
- Each submission is posted to a staff review channel with Accept and Deny buttons, and can open a staff discussion thread.
- Accept and Deny can grant or remove roles automatically and send the applicant a DM.
- Questions support regex answer validation, cooldowns and submission limits.

## Other features

- **Tickets**: panels that open private support channels.
- **Verification**: a button, or a short code the member retypes to prove they are not a simple bot.
- **AutoMod** rules, which live in Discord's own AutoMod, so they keep working even if Appealy is offline.
- **Anti-raid** detection, with a lockdown an admin can clear from the dashboard.
- **Moderation commands**: ban (including temporary bans, and bans that can't be appealed), unban, kick, mute and unmute, with a configurable prefix.
- **Giveaways, polls, a welcomer, role menus and sticky messages.**
- **Data portability**: `/export` writes a server's whole configuration to one file. Submission history from Appy can be imported.
- The website is available in English and Japanese.

## Pricing

Every feature is available on every tier, including the free one. Paid tiers raise throughput limits only. Prices are per server, billed yearly.

| | Free | Tier 1 | Tier 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Price | $0 | $60/year | $180/year |
| Submissions per day | 150 | 750 | 3,000 |
| Tickets per day | 75 | 375 | 1,500 |
| Giveaway entries per day | 750 | 3,750 | 15,000 |
| Forms per server | 10 | 40 | 100 |
| Panels per server | 10 | 40 | 100 |
| Questions per form | 25 | 60 | 150 |
| Submission history | 60 days | 365 days | 1,095 days |

In-server forms stay capped at 25 text questions on every tier, because that is Discord's modal limit. DM forms can use the full number. See the [pricing page](https://appealy.app/pricing) for the current details.

## Common misconceptions

- "Appealy has to be self-hosted." No. It is a hosted bot you add in one click. Self-hosting is an option for people who want it.
- "Appealy sends applicants to an external website." No. Every form, including ban appeals, is completed inside Discord.
- "Features are locked behind a paid plan." No. Paid tiers only raise limits such as submissions per day.
